headline: Senate Passes Bill Barring Officials’ Relatives From Government Contracts
seoTitle: Senate Passes Kin-Contract Ban Bill | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine Senate approved Senate Bill No. 1962 on third and final reading, seeking to bar relatives of covered public officials within the fourth civil degree from government contracts.
deck: Senate Bill No. 1962 cleared third and final reading, 15–0, as lawmakers moved to tighten conflict-of-interest rules in government contracting.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Senate approved Senate Bill No. 1962, the proposed Government Contracting and Procurement Integrity Act, on third and final reading on September 2, 2026.

The measure received 15 affirmative votes, with no negative vote and no abstention. It would prohibit relatives within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity of covered public officials and personnel from participating in or entering into government contracts where the covered relationship applies.

The prohibition would also reach certain subcontracting, consortium, joint-venture and similar arrangements connected to government contracts. Private entities seeking government deals would be required to make sworn disclosures on prohibited relationships involving officers, directors, trustees and beneficial owners.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The bill is designed to strengthen safeguards against conflicts of interest in public procurement and would amend relevant provisions of Republic Act No. 12009, the New Government Procurement Act.

During deliberations, senators also flagged possible unintended effects if the language is read too broadly. Senate leaders said those concerns, including whether some permits, leases or other government transactions could be swept into the measure, should be clarified during bicameral conference deliberations.
The bill is not yet law. It must still complete the legislative process, including reconciliation with a House counterpart and presidential action if Congress approves a final version.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Government procurement involves public money used for infrastructure, supplies, services and public-private projects. Rules that reduce opportunities for undisclosed family conflicts can directly affect competition, project quality and public trust.

The measure also matters because its scope is broad. If enacted, businesses seeking government contracts would face new disclosure and compliance duties, while covered officials and private parties could face criminal and administrative consequences for violations.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The key next step is the House of Representatives and any bicameral conference needed to reconcile the Senate measure with counterpart legislation.

Watch for revisions to the bill’s definition of covered contracts and transactions, the final list of covered officials and personnel, and whether the fourth-degree prohibition is retained in the final enrolled bill.
